intro: An attribute is anything that modifies a noun, and formal German stacks them. To the left of the noun (Linksattribute): articles, adjectives, participles and their complements — die kürzlich veröffentlichte Studie. To the right (Rechtsattribute): the genitive attribute (die Entscheidung der Kommission), the prepositional attribute (die Forderung nach Reformen), the apposition — a second noun phrase in the same case, set off by commas (Dr. Weber, die Leiterin des Instituts; mit Dr. Weber, der Leiterin — dative agrees), adverbs (das Haus dort), infinitive clauses (der Plan umzuziehen) and relative clauses. They chain: die kürzlich veröffentlichten Ergebnisse der Studie des Instituts zum Klima — participle, genitive, genitive, preposition. Reading such a phrase means finding the head noun (Ergebnisse) and hanging the rest on it; writing it means keeping the chain short — replace one genitive with a compound (der Institutsstudie) or move one attribute into a relative clause. Academic and official texts are built from these chains; in your own writing a chain that collapses loses the reader.
tips[0].title: Right attributes: genitive, preposition, apposition
tips[0].text: die Entscheidung der Kommission (Gen) · die Forderung nach Reformen (Präp) · Dr. Weber, die Leiterin des Instituts (Apposition, same case, commas) · mit Dr. Weber, der Leiterin des Instituts (dative apposition — the article agrees).
tips[0].trap: the apposition takes the case of the noun it explains: mit Dr. Weber, DER Leiterin (dative), not 'die Leiterin'. English has no case to match, so learners leave it nominative.
tips[0].check.why: The apposition takes the case of the noun it explains; mit Herrn Roth is dative, so: dem Direktor.
tips[1].title: Left attributes and the chain
tips[1].text: die | kürzlich veröffentlichten | Ergebnisse | der Studie | des Instituts | zum Klima. Head noun: Ergebnisse. Everything left of it is a participle phrase; everything right of it hangs on the previous noun in turn. Read: find the head, then peel outward.
tips[1].check.why: Everything between die and Reformen is a participle phrase describing it; des Verkehrssystems hangs on Reformen from the right.
tips[2].title: Shorten a chain: compound or relative clause
tips[2].text: die Ergebnisse der Studie des Instituts → die Ergebnisse der Institutsstudie (compound) · die von der Kommission getroffene Entscheidung → die Entscheidung, die die Kommission getroffen hat (relative clause). Two genitives in a row is the limit for readable prose.
tips[2].check.why: The relative pronoun agrees with die Maßnahme and is the accusative object here (die), and the finite verb goes to the end of the relative clause.
tips[3].title: Head noun first — always
tips[3].text: In any German noun phrase, the head is the first noun after the last adjective/participle. Find it, and the rest sorts itself: left = describing, right = belonging / relating.
tips[3].check.why: Plan is the head: vom Minister sits inside the participle phrase on the left, and the prepositional attribute on the right attaches to the head.

remember[0]: Left: adjectives, participles. Right: genitive, preposition, apposition (same case, commas), adverb, infinitive, relative clause.
remember[1]: Chains: find the head; shorten with a compound or a relative clause.
